summary.text: An embryo is the initial stage of development for a multicellular organism.
In sexually reproducing organisms it begins just after fertilization, when the fused egg and sperm form a single-celled zygote that divides into cells known as blastomeres.
Through gastrulation, which forms three germ layers, then neurulation and organogenesis, the embryo develops the tissues and organs of the body.

facts.label: Human embryo window
facts.value: Called an embryo until the ninth week after conception

facts.label: Germ layers
facts.value: Ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm form during gastrulation

facts.label: During cleavage
facts.value: Cells shrink and multiply while the embryo's size stays the same

facts.label: Zebrafish endpoint
facts.value: Embryonic development ends when the cleithrum bone appears

facts.label: Plant first division
facts.value: Asymmetric, giving one small apical and one large basal cell

items.prompt: A researcher traces an animal's skin and its nervous system back to the earliest embryo and finds they come from the same germ layer. Which one?
items.explain: The ectoderm gives rise to the skin epidermis and the nervous system.

items.prompt: Embryos of cnidarians form only two germ layers during gastrulation, while flatworms and humans form three. What term describes the cnidarians?
items.explain: Animals that form two layers are called diploblastic, and those that form three are called triploblastic.

items.prompt: After fertilization a zygote divides many times, yet the embryo's overall size does not change. What happens to the individual cells?

options.label: They quickly grow large to fill the space
They fuse together into fewer cells
They keep their size while the embryo shrinks
They get smaller as their number rises

items.explain: During cleavage the overall size stays the same, but individual cells shrink rapidly as they divide to increase the total number.

items.prompt: Why can't one rule decide when every animal stops being called an embryo?

options.label: The embryonic period varies from species to species
Only humans have an embryonic period at all
Birds stay embryos for their whole lives
Species disagree about whether fertilization occurs

items.explain: In humans the term fetus replaces embryo after the ninth week, while in zebrafish the embryonic period ends when the cleithrum becomes visible.

items.prompt: The offspring of a viviparous animal develops inside a parent's body. When is it typically no longer called an embryo?

options.label: Once its first cell division finishes
As soon as its organs begin to form
After birth or exit from the parent

items.explain: In viviparous animals the offspring is called an embryo while inside the parent and not after birth or exit.

items.prompt: What part of a seed feeds the growing plant embryo?
items.explain: The endosperm is nutrient-rich tissue that supports the growing plant embryo, while the seed coat is a protective outer covering.
